study: docs/DEBT.md item 142 — cross-fitted post-hoc layers, season 2425

no_2526_labels_read.method: fd_*_2526.csv files are not copied into load_matches' input dir

design.blocks: 5 contiguous chronological blocks per artifact (np.array_split of the kickoff-sorted rows)
design.kfold5: each block predicted by post-hoc layers fitted on the other 4
design.forward: block b (b=2..5) predicted by layers fitted on blocks < b; block 1 is never scored
design.C5_calibrator: sigmoid fitted on the training blocks' base-learner average (float32), applied to C4 — the served design
design.bootstrap: paired, ISO calendar-week blocks, 2000 replicates, seed 42; statistic = mean RPS delta over resampled rows
design.parity: 20 random rows (seed 42) per artifact vs PredictionEngine._run_inference (4 dp) and its unrounded success path; tolerance 1e-06

functions_used.shipped_calibrator_fitter: backend/scripts/train_on_real_matches.py@f1be78f^:1008 _fit_served_base_calibrator (sigmoid forced; its selection_rationale string is the one every shipped calibrator carries) -> calibration.fit_calibrator('sigmoid', y, base_average.astype(float32)). HEAD's version (backend/scripts/train_on_real_matches.py:1110) calls compare_calibration_methods, which selects on the holdout season, so it is not used here.

eredivisie.population: pooled artifact: every league's 2425 rows in train_pooled's order (Eredivisie has no pre-2526 season, so 0 of these rows are Eredivisie)

caveats: The scale-layer TYPE per league (temperature; vector for Ligue 1) was chosen by _select_calibrator, which consulted 2526. It is held fixed as shipped; only its parameters are refit out-of-fold here.

The Eredivisie artifact is the pooled model. Its 2425 population is the five other leagues' rows (Eredivisie has no pre-2526 season), so it is reported separately and excluded from the pooled row, which would otherwise score those rows twice.
Each out-of-fold layer is fitted on 4/5 of one season (forward: as little as 1/5), while the shipped layers used all of it; cross-fitted scores carry that small-sample cost.

Local runtime is Python 3.14 / scikit-learn 1.8; production is 3.11 / 1.3.2. The sigmoid calibrator is applied from coefficients (calibration._platt_probability), so the served numbers do not depend on the scikit-learn version.
No recommendation is made. Item 142's options remain an operator decision.
